newsitem.title: USA: PSE&G N.J. nuke nears restart after 2-year outage.
newsitem.headline: PSE&G N.J. nuke nears restart after 2-year outage.

text.p: Newark, New Jersey-based Public Service Electric and Gas Co is taking the final steps needed to restart its Salem 2 nuclear power plant, the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) said Monday.
The 1,106 megawatt (MW) unit was shut two years ago while its owners grappled with a series of operational and safety concerns linked to the plant.

The NRC's daily report on the operating status of the nation's nuclear power facilities said Salem 2 was now in "hot shutdown", which means its reactor has been reactivated but it is not yet producing electricity.

The report also gives a tentative date of July 11 for its resumption of power production. The actual restart date hinges on when the unit, undergoing extensive testing and inspection, is finally cleared by the NRC to resume operation.
PSE&G said earlier that it planned to run the plant at low power levels for several weeks for testing.
The adjacent unit, Salem 1, rated at the same capacity and off line since May, 1995, is slated to restart in November, according to the report.
PSE&G is the operator and co-owner of both Salem units. Other owners include PECO Energy Co, Delmarva Power and Light Co and Atlantic Energy Co.
